query: Consider the following context: Materials capable of withstanding extreme environments open promising opportunities for nuclear fusion reactors. In that context, which material can be used for interlayer materials between W and CuCrZr, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Tungsten carbide (WC) can be used as an interlayer material between tungsten (W) and copper-chromium-zirconium (CuCrZr) due to its high thermal conductivity, mechanical strength, and compatibility with both materials.
generation.material_initial_state: Tungsten (W) and copper-chromium-zirconium (CuCrZr) in their bulk forms
generation.intervention: Deposition of a 10-20 μm thick tungsten carbide (WC) interlayer between W and CuCrZr using chemical vapor deposition (CVD) at 1000°C
generation.structural_mediator: The WC interlayer's crystalline structure and grain size
generation.mechanism: The WC interlayer enhances thermal conductivity and reduces thermal stress between W and CuCrZr, thereby improving the overall performance and lifespan of the material system
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20-30% increase in thermal conductivity and a 15-25% reduction in thermal stress compared to the W-CuCrZr system without the WC interlayer
generation.baseline: The thermal conductivity and thermal stress of the W-CuCrZr system without the WC interlayer
generation.boundary: The WC interlayer's thickness and deposition conditions
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the WC interlayer may vary depending on the specific deposition conditions, operating temperature, and pressure

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the thermal conductivity and thermal stress of the W-WC-CuCrZr system and compare it to the W-CuCrZr system without the WC interlayer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity increase is less than 10% or the thermal stress reduction is less than 5%, the hypothesis is falsified
